images.alt: A KC 85/4 home computer in its case, photographed from the front showing the keyboard and cassette port
images.caption: The KC 85/4 shipped in 1988 from VEB Mikroelektronik in Mühlhausen, Thuringia, the last major revision of the line.
images.author: Kolossos

images.alt: A KC 85 series East German home computer displayed with its keyboard, photographed for a museum or collection
images.caption: Most KC 85/4 units went where the state plan sent them — schools and after-school technical clubs — rather than to private buyers.
images.author: stiefkind

images.alt: A KC 85 home computer on display, shown with its case and keyboard in a technical collection
images.caption: Inside was a U880, an East German Z80 clone built without a licence from Zilog.
images.author: Dr. Bernd Gross

images.alt: A KC 85 series East German home computer, photographed showing its full case and keyboard
images.caption: The machine's slots let it grow: RAM and ROM modules, a floppy interface, an assembler, all pushed into the side of the case.
images.author: Wolfgang Stief from Tittmoning, Germany

images.alt: A KC 85 series computer with its keyboard and case visible, photographed at an angle
images.caption: CAOS, the Cassette Aided Operating System, prints its own command menu at power-on so the first screen is also the documentation.
images.author: Wolfgang Stief from Tittmoning, Germany
